haiku-low.q1: It does not differ. Both return HTTP 401 and the login page showing "Invalid email or password", so nothing reveals whether an account exists.
haiku-low.q2: It gets HTTP 429 with Retry-After and "Too many failed attempts. Please try again later." The password is not checked and the attempt is not recorded as a failure.
haiku-low.q3: On successful login the old session is deleted and a brand-new session ID is issued. Failed or locked attempts leave any existing session untouched.
haiku-low.q4: Only an opaque random session ID, in cookie sid with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax and Path=/. HttpOnly means page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: At 12 hours after login. Each request restarts the 30-minute idle clock, but created_at is never updated, so the 12-hour absolute limit still applies.
haiku-low.q6: It redirects to /login and clears the cookie with Max-Age=0. It also makes a best-effort delete of that session row; the failure is only logged.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session row and commits before replying, then clears the cookie and redirects to /login. If no session exists, the response is identical.
haiku-low.q8: In shared Postgres tables, in the sessions table keyed by the SHA-256 hash of the cookie value. Any instance queries the same database, so it finds the session.
haiku-low.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table, one row per failed attempt with attempted_at. The count uses attempted_at greater than now() minus 10 minutes, based on timestamps.
haiku-low.q10: It compares the hashed cookie with a row whose last_seen_at is within 30 minutes and created_at within 12 hours, using Postgres now(). If valid, it writes last_seen_at = now().
haiku-low.q11: HTTP 503 with the login page saying "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Please try again." No Set-Cookie is sent, and the old session remains untouched.
haiku-low.q12: A background sweep timer in each app instance, run at startup and every 10 minutes, deletes expired sessions, old login_failures and expired lockouts.

sonnet.q1: They don't differ. Both get HTTP 401 and the login page showing "Invalid email or password". The unknown-email case runs bcrypt against a dummy hash so timing is about the same.
sonnet.q2: It is refused with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header (whole seconds), plus the login page message "Too many failed attempts. Please try again later." The password is not checked and the attempt is not recorded as a failure. The lock lasts 15 minutes.
sonnet.q3: On a successful login, the session the incoming cookie pointed to is deleted in the same transaction, and a brand-new session with a new random ID is issued. A failed (401) or locked (429) login leaves the existing session untouched.
sonnet.q4: Only the opaque random session ID (cookie sid). It is flagged HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. It is also Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/.
sonnet.q5: After 12 hours from login, the absolute limit, even with continuous use. The 30-minute idle limit never triggers because every request restarts the idle clock.
sonnet.q6: No row matches, so the server treats it as no session. It makes a best-effort DELETE of that session row (failure is logged and ignored). It then clears the cookie (sid= with Max-Age=0) and redirects to /login.
sonnet.q7: If there is a cookie, the server runs DELETE FROM sessions for that hash and commits it before replying. It then clears the cookie and redirects to /login. If the session is already gone, the delete is a no-op and the response is identical. With no cookie, the database is skipped.
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres sessions table, which both instances share. The instance hashes the cookie value (SHA-256 of the UTF-8 string, raw 32 bytes) and looks up id_hash with an UPDATE ... RETURNING user_id.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table, with one row per failed attempt, keyed by the normalized email. The server counts rows where attempted_at > now() - interval '10 minutes', using the database clock. The count does not depend on the sweep having run.
sonnet.q10: It checks that last_seen_at is within 30 minutes of now() (idle limit) and that created_at is within 12 hours of now() (absolute limit), all in the one UPDATE. When valid, it writes last_seen_at = now(). created_at is never updated.
sonnet.q11: HTTP 503 and the login page saying "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Please try again." There is no Set-Cookie and no session is issued.
sonnet.q12: The periodic sweep, run by a timer in each app instance on startup and every 10 minutes. It deletes sessions with last_seen_at older than 30 minutes or created_at older than 12 hours. Lazy deletion also happens when a request arrives with an unknown or expired cookie.
